title: The Critical note in the margin
subtitle: 竞技体育 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 竞技体育（文学艺术与体育·竞技体育与赛事）
meta: 主题语境：竞技体育（文学艺术与体育·竞技体育与赛事）　|　核心词汇：critical　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 critical 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1953 the musician wrote of ① a critical note in the margin in the programme, and everybody in the hall said at once that it was ② more critical than the one named there the year before. Three nights on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the musician, who never explained anything, had done it on the same day and gone home; it was the critical ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the most critical note in the margin anybody in the hall had ever seen, or so the programme for December 1947 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too critical to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the listener who had come to help; the critical ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the score at the far piano, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a critical moment in the game, and said that no listener in his right mind would call it ⑥ as critical as the moment in the game they had once had in the old hall. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was critical or not, and he said so.

By 1960 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the programme. What the line asked for was ⑦ something critical, and nothing besides. The listener from the next hall called the whole plan ⑧ quite critical; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the programme kept the names of the critical ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1963, before dawn, she wrote of another critical note in the margin in the same programme, and the work, which took two nights, seemed ⑨ more critical than anybody had expected. ⑩ The most critical moment in the game in the whole hall, she said in 1965, was the one she could never quite name; the critical ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 批评（前置定语 a critical note in the margin：1953 年乐师在节目单里记下的那件批评的评语）
B. adj. 批评／关键（比较级 more critical than：文中两处，一处比页边的评语，一处比预想）
C. adj. 批评／关键（最高级 the most critical：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 批评（表语 too critical to do：母亲觉得它太批评，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 关键（前置定语 a critical moment in the game：叔叔把整件事称作一桩关键的时刻）
F. adj. 关键（同级比较 as critical as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩比赛的关键时刻相比）
G. adj. 关键（后置定语 something critical：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 关键（受程度副词修饰 quite critical：那位听客的评价）

items.q: a critical note in the margin
the most critical note in the margin anybody
a critical moment in the game
The most critical moment in the game in

answers.why: critical 意为“批评”，1953 年乐师在节目单里记下的是“一件批评的评语”，此处作前置定语 a critical note in the margin。
critical 意为“批评”，此处用比较级 more critical than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
critical 意为“批评”，节目单上 十二月 那行字说它是音乐厅里最批评的一件，故用最高级 the most critical note in the margin。
critical 意为“批评”，母亲认为这件东西“太批评了，谁也用不上”，too critical to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
critical 意为“关键”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩关键的时刻”，此处作前置定语 a critical moment in the game。
critical 意为“关键”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩比赛的关键时刻一样关键”，同级比较用 as critical as。
critical 意为“关键”，节目单上那半行字要的是“关键的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something critical。
critical 意为“关键”，邻音乐厅来的那位听客认为这套计划“相当关键”，quite 修饰原级 critical。
critical 意为“关键”，1963 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要关键”，故用比较级 more critical than。
critical 意为“关键”，母亲 1965 年说的是“整个音乐厅里最关键的那一桩”，故用最高级 the most critical moment in the game。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1953 年，乐师在节目单里记下了一件批评的评语。（a critical note in the margin）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更批评。（more critical than …）
母亲觉得它太批评，谁也用不上。（too critical to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩关键的时刻。（a critical moment in the game）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩比赛的关键时刻一样关键。（as critical as …）
到了 1960 年，节目单上只剩半行字：要的是一件关键的东西。（something critical）
answers: In 1953 the musician wrote of a critical note in the margin in the programme.
Everybody said it was more critical than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too critical to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a critical moment in the game.
He said nobody would call it as critical as the moment in the game they had once had.
By 1960 the programme asked for nothing but something critical.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 critical 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1953 the musician wrote of a critical note in the margin in the programme, and nobody forgot it.
It was the most critical note in the margin in the hall, or so the programme says.
My mother thought it too critical to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a critical moment in the game, and nobody argued with him.
The listener from the next hall called the plan quite critical, and everybody laughed.
The critical ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
